detail: `val or default` is falsy when val=0.0/0, silently reverting to default. Use `if val is None: val = default` (image-faceswap, image-expansion, image-i2i seed). Run 2026-06-21T17-06-24 (FIX tier) APPLIED the fix at app/commands/_shared.py:140 seed_sequence: replaced `seed = getattr(args_or_config, 'seed', None) or 777` with explicit `if seed is None: seed = 777`. The pytest restore lane reverted ONLY the test file. LESSON: when fixing the `or` falsy-coalesce, the seed=0 semantics genuinely CHANGE — audit every test asserting the old 'seed=0 -> default' behavior and update the test contract, not the fix. Sibling to MEMORY argparse-sentinel-for-user-override.

title: Unguarded default=None on a flag silently wins over _shared's intended concrete default (e.g. default=777) on the unified image parser
detail: image-profile.py registers --seed with default=None but does NOT guard it, so the None silently overrides the _shared default=777 on the unified image parser. This is the same sentinel-pattern bug family already documented in MEMORY (argparse-sentinel-for-user-override): a per-command flag without a guard (default=None treated as 'unset') collides with the shared parser's concrete default. Here it manifests as the shared default being shadowed rather than as a magic-number override, but the root cause — missing guard so the per-command registration participates in arg resolution — is identical. Confirmed AGAIN run 2026-06-21T00-11-24 (image-profile.py, high severity): profile --seed default=None still poisons --seed for ALL image sub-actions on the unified parser. The fact that it keeps being flagged at HIGH severity and was independently recorded in MEMORY (argparse-sentinel-for-user-override) marks it as one of the most durable bug-families in this codebase. Run 2026-06-21T17-06-24 re-confirmed the sibling image-i2i.py site: seed=getattr(args,'seed',42) returns None when the --seed default=None leaked, silently disabling np.random.seed (high).

title: Subcommand registers shared flags WITHOUT guards, relying on _shared's LATER skip to dedupe — order-coupled and fragile; stale comments compound it
detail: video-generate.py:192 declares --lora-path/--lora-scale/--prompt/--seed unguarded and depends on _shared.add_common_generation_args() skipping already-registered flags when it runs afterward. Correctness hinges entirely on registration ORDER (subcommand before _shared) and on _shared's skip logic being present. If _shared ever runs first, or its skip is removed/changed, these become argparse 'conflicting option' errors or silent double-registration. Run 2026-06-19 re-surfaced two facets: image.py:289 duplicate shared flags (--film-grain/--sharpening/--seed/--output) rely on registration ORDER not guards (medium), and video.py:113 stale comment claims --self-test is registered by add_common_generation_args() which video.py never calls (low). Run 2026-06-21 re-surfaced a third facet: image-workflow.py registers --film-grain / --sharpening without a guard, so purify's guarded copies of the same flags are silently skipped (help-text divergence between the two registrations). This is an architectural smell, not always a live crash today. Run 2026-06-21T02-22-56 re-surfaced FOUR more facets at once: image-profile.py --ref-strength (survives only via call-order coupling with anime2real), image-workflow.py --film-grain/--sharpening (purify must run AFTER workflow), image-t2i.py --resolution (image-purify guarded --resolution order-coupled), image-review.py --output (order-coupled to purify's guarded --output) — confirming this is the dominant argparse hotspot family across the codebase. Run 2026-06-21T17-06-24 re-confirmed image.py:223 (unified image parser relies on registration ORDER for shared-flag default precedence — fragile, no enforcement) as the architectural root.

detail: image-anime2real.py:156: --realism-style help string claims '3d-game (default)' but the actual argparse default is civitai-chinese. Pure documentation drift — help text was not updated when the default changed. No runtime impact, but erodes trust in --help and the schema-defaults reflection. Run 2026-06-21 re-surfaced a sibling: image-t2i.py help text advertises default 640/960 but the argparse default is None (sentinel) — same docs-vs-argparse-default drift class, only the dimensions differ. Run 2026-06-21T02-22-56 re-surfaced a third sibling: image-profile.py:152 STALE COMMENT (not help text) claims shared --seed default is 42 while the actual shared default is 777 — the drift class now spans help strings AND inline comments; grep both when a shared default changes.

title: Reshape/downsample expressions that assume dims are exact multiples of the latent grid, hidden behind an obfuscated one-liner
detail: flux2_outpaint_pipeline.py:330: mask downsample reshape assumes spatial dims are exact multiples of the latent grid, but the expression is written as an obfuscated one-liner that hides the divisibility assumption. If a caller passes dims that are NOT clean multiples (e.g. odd outpaint targets), the reshape silently produces wrong-shaped tensors or crashes with a cryptic error. Refactor to an explicit assert or floor-div with a comment stating the invariant. Low severity because current call paths happen to satisfy it; latent trap for future callers.

title: args.lora_scale is a LIST (multi-LoRA action=append) but call sites pass it as a scalar lora_scale — nested list / dataclass field violation
detail: With multi-LoRA support, args.lora_scale is registered with action="append" so it is always a list. Several command call sites pass the whole list where a scalar float is expected, producing a nested list or a dataclass type violation. Confirmed in run 2026-06-19T22-02-33 across THREE files: image-faceswap.py:438 wraps args.lora_scale (list) into lora_scales=[lora_scale] → nested list lora_scales=[[...]] passed to Flux2KleinPipeline; image-expansion.py:325 assigns whole args.lora_scale list to scalar lora_scale; image-workflow.py:877 builds RunConfig with lora_scale as a list, violating the float dataclass field. Sibling family to correctness:lora-path-list-vs-string-resolve (same root cause: multi-LoRA list not unwrapped at call sites). Fix shape: index the list or have pipelines accept a list consistently. Run 2026-06-21T02-22-56 NEW facet: app/commands/_shared.py:245 --lora-scale is registered as action=append (list) but this registration LEAKS into the VIDEO pipelines, which expect a scalar float — the list-not-scalar surface is NOT confined to the image sub-actions; the shared registration poisons video too. Run 2026-06-21T17-06-24 (FIX tier) APPLIED a fix at video-vbvr.py:364: added inline list-peeling before LTXVideoPipeline construction (args.lora_scale list -> scalar when action=append) — the video-pipeline facet is now guarded at vbvr; other call sites remain unguarded.

title: A concrete default on a per-subcommand flag wins for ALL sibling sub-actions on the unified image parser (first-writer-wins poisoning)
detail: image-purify.py:85 (run 2026-06-20): --seed is registered with default=42 inside purify's add_args, but because image uses a unified parser, that concrete default wins for EVERY image sub-action, overriding the intended t2i default seed=777. Distinct from the default=None sentinel family (argparse-integrity:unguarded-default-none-overrides-shared): there the per-command flag lacks a guard; here the per-command flag sets a CONCRETE default that leaks across sub-actions. Root cause: unified parser + per-submodule add_args means any concrete default a submodule sets becomes global to the parser. Run 2026-06-21T02-22-56 NEW site: app/commands/image-i2i.py:295 denoise_strength default=0.4 leaks onto the unified image parser, overriding the shared default=1.0 — same first-writer-wins concrete-default-leak class, now affecting a DIFFERENT flag (denoise_strength) than seed. Run 2026-06-21T17-06-24 re-confirmed the rejected sibling (image-i2i.py denoise_strength 0.4 leak + image-profile --seed default=None leak) — both rejected as already-recorded, confirming stable signatures. Fix shape: register shared flags once in _shared with the canonical default, and have submodules skip (or use default=None + guard) rather than re-declaring with a concrete value.

title: OpenCV VideoCapture / native handles opened without try/finally leak the handle if later code raises
detail: cv2.VideoCapture() (and VideoWriter) is opened and read, but cap.release() sits on the happy path with no try/finally — if any line between open and release raises, the capture handle is never released (fd/camera lock leaks, and on some backends the file stays locked). Same resource-lifetime class as mlx-review:image-open-without-context-manager but for OpenCV native handles rather than PIL files. Fix shape: wrap in try/finally (or contextlib.ExitStack) so release always runs. Hotspots across runs: video-segment.py (cap.get), video-restore.py (VideoCapture + VideoWriter, run 2026-06-21T00-11-24 medium).

title: add_review_args registers --output unguarded, conflicting with purify/other --output registrations (first-writer-wins)
detail: image-review.py:134 (run 2026-06-20): add_review_args() registers --output without checking whether it is already registered, creating a semantic conflict with image-purify's --output (and any other submodule --output) on the unified image parser. First-writer-wins means whichever submodule loads first owns the --output dest. Same architectural smell as mlx-review:vbvr-duplicate-dest-registrations and mlx-review:purify-mode-dest-collision: shared dest names registered without coordination. Recurred run 2026-06-21T02-22-56 (image-review.py:134 unguarded --output order-coupled to purify's guarded --output). Run 2026-06-21T17-06-24 re-confirmed image-purify.py:153 --output registered by both purify and review on the unified image parser (medium). Fix shape: centralize --output (and other shared dests) in _shared with one canonical registration, or use add_argument with conflict_handler='resolve' deliberately.

title: image.py calls _restore.add_restore_args but 'restore' is not a documented image sub-action (dead registration)
detail: image.py invokes _restore.add_restore_args to register restore flags, but 'restore' is not listed as an image sub-action in COMMAND_NAMES / the image dispatcher, so the registration is dead — the flags are parsed but never routed to a handler. Same dead-registration family as mlx-review:animate-dead-code-command (orphan command module) but here the module IS reachable while the action wiring is not. Fix shape: either document 'restore' as an image sub-action and route it, or drop the add_restore_args call to stop advertising unreachable flags. Run 2026-06-21T00-11-24 (image.py:281, low).

title: _arg_registered() helper inspects parser._actions — a CPython-private attribute that can break across argparse versions
detail: app/commands/_shared.py:170 (run 2026-06-21T02-22-56): the _arg_registered() dedup-helper iterates parser._actions to detect already-registered flags. parser._actions is a private attribute (leading underscore); CPython/argparse give no stability guarantee for it across versions, so the dedup logic that the entire unified-parser order-coupling pattern depends on is itself built on a fragile foundation. If argparse ever renames or restructures _actions, every 'already registered, skip' guard silently stops deduping, converting all order-coupled skips into argparse 'conflicting option' crashes. Fix shape: prefer the public parse_known_args probe or track registered dests in an explicit set rather than reaching into _actions. Medium severity: latent today, but it is the load-bearing wall under the whole shared-flag skip architecture.

title: A/B variation generate() reuses args.input_image / args.audio across iterations — shared-state mutation yields correlated variants instead of independent ones
detail: app/commands/video-generate.py:1011 (run 2026-06-21T02-22-56, medium): the A/B variation loop's generate() calls all pass the SAME args.input_image / args.audio objects across iterations. If any iteration mutates those (e.g. a pipeline writes back into the image/audio, or a sub-step reassigns an attribute), subsequent variants inherit the mutation — the variants are no longer independent samples of the same config, they are a correlated chain. The bug is silent: outputs look different (seed differs) but share corrupted upstream state. Fix shape: deep-copy or re-resolve args.input_image / args.audio per iteration, or guarantee the generate() path never mutates them. This is the shared-state-mutation sibling to mlx-review:systemexit-aborts-variation-loop (both are variation-loop correctness traps). Run 2026-06-21T17-06-24 re-confirmed a sibling facet at app/run_config.py:111: ab_params typed as dict but shared across A/B variations WITHOUT deep copy (medium) — the same shared-state-mutation trap, now at the config layer (ab_params) not just the args layer.

title: A module duplicates symbols from the live source module but is imported ONLY by tests — production and tests silently diverge
detail: app/commands/_output.py and app/commands/_model_resolver.py each re-implement symbols that already live in app/commands/_shared.py (OutputPaths, generate_base_name, make_output_paths, DEFAULT_UPSCALE_MODEL, RELAY_FINAL_MODE / resolve_lora_path, resolve_vae_path, _find_safetensors_in_dir, list_available_loras) but are imported ONLY by their dedicated test files. Result: production code evolves in _shared.py while the test-only copy stays frozen, so the tests assert behavior of a STALE duplicate and pass even when the live symbol changed — production and tests diverge with no signal. This is a STRUCTURAL false-confidence trap: green tests do NOT mean the live code works. Fix shape: delete the duplicate module and repoint the test imports at the live source (_shared.py). Run 2026-06-21T17-06-24 (FIX tier) APPLIED this: deleted _output.py + _model_resolver.py and rewrote test_commands__output.py / test_model_resolver.py to import from app.commands._shared; grep confirmed no production code imported either duplicate. Always grep for non-test importers before deleting; if a duplicate has a production importer, unify the implementation instead.

title: Smoke tests run against the DEPRECATED ComfyUI/.venv produce spurious t2i/image/animate/generate failures; the correct venv is python/venv
detail: Run 2026-06-21T17-06-24 baseline reported 'smoke 11 passed / 4 failed (t2i, image, animate, generate)' — these 4 failures were ARTIFACTS of invoking smoke against ComfyUI/.venv (the DEPRECATED, mlx-less venv). Re-running all 15 smoke commands against python/venv (the ACTIVE project venv with mlx installed) gives 15/15 exit 0 with NO 'ArgumentError: conflicting option string'. The pytest baseline (1000 passed, 0 pre-existing) was already measured against python/venv, so it matched reality; only the smoke lane was poisoned by the wrong env. LESSON: any smoke failure mentioning ModuleNotFoundError / mlx / mflux is almost certainly a wrong-venv artifact, NOT a regression — re-run smoke with python/venv/bin/python before trusting a smoke failure. The only genuine regression this run was test_seed_zero (pytest), which the restore lane caught. This is the workflow-runner analog of the mlx-movie-director-regression-suite MEMORY entry (clear __pycache__ + correct cwd) extended to the venv choice.
